pageCache.text:
Welcome to Westonbirt
Westonbirt School is a co-ed independent boarding and day school for boys and girls aged 2 to 18 years. Located in the Cotswolds, 90 minutes from London, here you will find an inspired community, set in 210 acres of parkland and a breathtaking mansion. We are guided by a deep belief in the endless potential of every child, which underpins our pursuit of excellence and the high expectations that we have of them.
Book a personal tour
Five star education
Nursery
Children can start their Westonbirt journey in the nursery from 2 years old. Nursery is a fundamental part of the Westonbirt community and follows the same values as the rest of the school with the matching aims of creating inspiring opportunities for learning and experiencing a joyous childhood.
Prep School
Westonbirt Prep offers co-ed learning from 2 to 11 years. Immersed in a culture that promotes a love of learning, children are encouraged to be curious, creative and courageous. Set within 210 acres of parkland grounds, pupils benefit from an abundance of outdoor space and the specialist teaching and facilities of a much larger school.
Senior School
Westonbirt Senior School is a co-educational independent day and boarding school for boys and girls aged 11 to 18 years. It was voted 'Co-educational Independent School of the Year' at the 2023 Independent School of the Year awards. We aim to develop young people who are compassionate and courageous, ready not only for university or the next stage of their education, but for exciting, fulfilling and productive lives well beyond their school years.
Sixth Form
Westonbirt offers a wide range of subjects and qualifications in the Sixth Form, including A levels, BTECs, Leiths, the EPQ and more. Students can tailor a bespoke programme of study to their individual skills and aspirations. Class sizes are small and students are supported to achieve their very best academically, with plenty of leadership and development opportunities available. 46% of grades in 2025 were at A*/A and 90% of students achieve their first-choice university; 2025 university destinations include Durham, Les Roches, University of Warwick, University of Exeter, Royal Holloway, and University of Liverpool.

Microsoft Outage
We have been affected by the worldwide Microsoft outage and have no access to emails or Teams. This means we will not have received any emails sent overnight and we will be unable to access or respond to emails until the service is restored. Parents can still phone the school, but please bear with us, as the phonelines are likely to be very busy.

Personalised Learning Pathways
Personalised Learning Pathways (PLP) really sets Westonbirt Prep apart from its competitors, giving pupils a truly individualised curriculum.
This bespoke programme delivers daily sessions tailored to every child from Year 3-Year 6. They allow us to support children where they need extra time, enrich their learning with new experiences and challenge them to stretch themselves in subjects where they excel.
It includes subjects as broad as maths, Italian, Latin, music and history’s mysteries, and fuels the children’s enthusiasm for learning.
What are Personalised Learning Pathways?
Each child from Year 3 to Year 6 is allocated a personalised timetable, assigning them to a 30-minute slot each day in addition to their class timetable. Groups range in size from roughly six to 16 children, depending on the session.
Sessions are split into three categories: Support, Challenge and Enrichment. Across the week, a child may have sessions from each of the three categories, or perhaps just two categories (e.g. Support and Enrichment, or Support and Challenge), depending on their individual timetable.
Example PLP Timetables
Key Features
Comprehensive Support
Each session is tailored to meet the individual needs of our pupils, providing them with the guidance and resources that they need to succeed.
Meaningful Challenges
We create opportunities for the children to engage in thought-provoking activities that push them to think critically and solve problems creatively.
Enriching Experiences
The PLP programme includes a variety of activities that cater to the diverse interests of our pupils, from art and sports, to languages and STEM.
Hear From Our Pupils
“I enjoy all the PLPs because I like spending time with different teachers and I get to try new things.” Sienna; Year 4
“History’s Mysteries encourages us to think for ourselves and research unsolved mysteries.” Bertie; Year 5
“I like Italian and Latin PLPs because I like learning new languages.” Henry; Year 4
“I like the Sport PLPs because they are fun and active.” Sam; Year 4
“The Computer Science PLP is my favourite because we get to use the Surface tablets.” Eva; Year 5
“Ensemble Choir is great because we learn different styles of music and various pieces of music throughout the year.” Henry; Year 6

pageCache.text:
The Westonbirt Prep advantage
At Westonbirt Prep, a lively and ambitious curriculum, a talented and ambitious team of staff, and senior-quality facilities in the glorious Gloucestershire countryside combine to create the perfect conditions for learning. This magical formula gives our children an advantage in developing and achieving their potential.
A curriculum to engage and challenge
Our experiential, hands-on curriculum immerses children in their education, grabbing their interest and holding their attention. A high staff-to-child ratio ensures children are expertly guided through their learning journey, supported where they need a leg up and stretched where their abilities show promise, to be the best they possibly can be. The result is a school full of students who are excited and enthused, a happy community of children who are motivated and excited to learn.
Highly qualified and enthusiastic teachers
And our staff? They are talented and enthusiastic, ambitious for our children, and keen to share a fascination for their subjects. Many teachers are senior-level subject specialists, and we have qualified teachers among our teaching assistants too, significantly elevating the quality of provision. They are here to guide, not control, to unlock the potential in every child, helping them focus their energies, encouraging exploration and discovery and developing their skills as lifelong learners. They allow children to make mistakes and face challenges, readying them for the road ahead.
Discover our Specialist Teaching
Outstanding facilities in a breathtaking setting
The third part of the puzzle is the beautiful Cotswold setting, and amazing facilities. Our 221-acre classroom stretches around us, a constant source of inspiration for learning and creativity. Within it are found specialist, senior-quality spaces for STEM, art, technology, music, swimming, physical education & games, and our pupils are able to make use of facilities that would normally be reserved for senior-age children.
Discover our Outdoor Learning opportunities
Making a strong start – Pre-Prep (4-7 years)
The heart of our Pre-Prep department is active engagement, curiosity and creativity.
Discover life in Reception
Forging ahead – Prep (age 7-11 years)
Whether it’s languages, literature or Lego robotics, Year 3 is where learning really becomes turbo powered. We have grasped their attention, and now is the time they will inhale all the learning we can deliver.
Discover the Westonbirt Edge
Personalised Learning Pathways
Personalised Learning Pathways (PLP) really sets Westonbirt Prep apart from its competitors, giving pupils a truly individualised curriculum. This bespoke programme delivers daily sessions tailored to every child from Year 3-Year 6. They allow us to support children where they need extra time, enrich their learning with new experiences and challenge them to stretch themselves in subjects where they excel. It includes subjects as broad as maths, Italian, Latin, music and history’s mysteries, and fuels the children’s enthusiasm for learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Festival of EPQ celebrates independent research - Westonbirt School
pageCache.text:
Festival of EPQ celebrates independent research
Our Upper Sixth pupils recently had the opportunity to showcase their Extended Project Qualifications at our Festival of EPQ, celebrating months of independent research and academic exploration.
The EPQ complements pupils’ Sixth Form studies while giving them the opportunity to take ownership of a substantial piece of independent work. Through planning, researching and presenting their projects, pupils develop skills in critical thinking, academic research, organisation and communication.
The Festival of EPQ brought together pupils, parents and guests for an evening showcasing the breadth and depth of the projects. Each pupil created a topic stand and presented their research, sharing what they had discovered as well as what they had learned from undertaking such an extended piece of independent study.
The projects explored an impressive range of questions, including the reliability of fossil evidence in reconstructing dinosaur behaviour, the expansion of Roman power, nostalgic triggers across generations, the future of motorsport and the role of fungi in Western medicine.
Other projects investigated whether the adversarial system is the best way to deliver justice, the extent to which the UK can rely on renewable energy in the future, and whether it is possible to have intellectual, human-level conversations with animals.
‘The Festival of EPQ gave our brilliant Upper Sixth cohort the opportunity to showcase the results of a year of ambitious and independent work,’ said Imogen Morris, Head of Upper Sixth. ‘The evening was a wonderful celebration of the pupils’ curiosity, commitment and intellectual ambition. Parents were particularly impressed by the breadth of topics explored and the depth of knowledge that pupils had developed through their research. Their presentations also provided an inspiring glimpse of what awaits our current Lower Sixth pupils, who will soon embark on their own EPQ projects.’

Welcome to Westonbirt Nursery
Through free play, formal learning and great outdoor experiences, Westonbirt Nursery encourages creativity, curiosity, confidence and fun – as well as a lifelong love for learning and exploring. Our core programme is supplemented by a range of exciting and dynamic extra-curricular activities that are led by specialist teachers including music, French, games, swimming and forest school.
Meet The Head
Westonbirt Nursery welcomes children from 2 years through to pre-school. The Nursery is a vibrant and positive setting where the happiness of the children is our priority. The location allows for extensive use of our wonderful outdoor space and exploring nature and the wider world is a large part of the Westonbirt experience.
Children learn primarily through play and follow the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum; they begin to build their understanding of numbers, sounds and language with daily sessions that build through their time with us from 2 years old to the preparation for transition to school phase. This phase focuses on giving the children an opportunity to develop independence and confidence, as well as key skills such as writing, holding cutlery, getting themselves changed and following routines and expectations.
The school aims of Curiosity, Creativity and Courage are prevalent in all that happens in Nursery and this stands children in good stead to move on in their educational journey.
Contact our admissions team to book a taster session or join us for our next Open Day. This is an excellent opportunity to talk to the dedicated nursery staff about our ethos and educational provision and discuss how our flexible morning and afternoon sessions can best meet your needs:
Q & A
How old must my child be to attend Westonbirt Nursery?
Westonbirt Nursery is open to children aged 2-4 years old.
Is parking available at Westonbirt Nursery?
Westonbirt School's main car park is located next to Westonbirt Nursery. Dedicated drop-off bays for Westonbirt Prep and Westonbirt Nursery are also available for use in the morning and afternoon, located directly outside the nursery.
Does Westonbirt Nursery accept Government funding?
Westonbirt Nursery accept up to 15 hours’ free childcare entitlement per week for up to 38 weeks of the year. For those registered for term-time only, we offer 15 hours per week for the total weeks attended. Those registered for a year-round place will receive their free hours pro-rated over the three funding periods (1st Sept – 31st Dec; 1st Jan – 31st Mar; 1st Apr – 31st Aug). We also accept childcare vouchers to pay for nursery care.
What time does Westonbirt Nursery open and close?
Westonbirt Nursery is open from 8am-6pm, Monday to Friday.
Is Westonbirt Nursery open all year round?
Westonbirt Nursery year runs from September to August. We accept pupils for either school term time only or for the whole year. Term time only pupils may book additional ad-hoc nursery sessions during the school holidays, subject to places being available.
What is the minimum number of sessions I can book at Westonbirt Nursery?
We require a minimum attendance of 2 full days per week to join the nursery.
Is food included in Westonbirt Nursery fees?
Westonbirt Nursery fees include all food and consumables required to support our provision. We also offer a wide range of activities during the nursery week; these are all included in the session rates where these are paid. If using free childcare entitlement, you will be asked to pay towards the cost of food and consumables, and for some activities where funding does not meet the cost. Please view our full Nursery Fees Information here.
How do I visit Westonbirt Nursery?
Contact our Admissions Team via nurseryadmissions@westonbirtschool.uk or 01666 881400 to book a individual visit to Westonbirt Nursery. You can also register to attend our Prep School and Nursery Open Mornings, which take place in the autumn and spring.

Specialist Teaching
Pupils at Westonbirt Prep benefit from a wide range of specialist teaching from the very earliest stages in their education. With access to teachers and specialist facilities shared with the senior school, these experiences are designed to ignite passions and inspiration and to allow children the opportunity to try new things, learn new skills and be challenged in a variety of ways.
Specialist teaching and facilities
In Reception, children are taught French, Forest School, music, PE and swimming alongside their core subjects and wider curriculum. These subjects are delivered by specialist teachers and we make the most of facilities across the campus and in the senior school, such as the Orangery Theatre, the leisure centre and swimming pool and the music studios.
As children progress through the prep school, there is an increase in specialist-delivered provision to cover art, drama, computing, science and STEM, in addition to the specialist-delivered subjects studied at pre-prep. These lessons make use dedicated facilities and are vital in preparing children with both the knowledge and skills for senior education and beyond.
Performing Arts
Every child across the school benefits from at least one weekly lesson in performing arts taught by a subject specialist teacher. Our performing arts team delivers a curriculum that allows children to learn theory, to explore and create using their own ideas and a variety of mediums and to perform in a multitude of different contexts. They use the shared facilities of the Orangery Theatre and music studios to enhance their experience and allow for the best delivery possible.
Drama and music focus on inspiring the children and giving them the chance to enjoy the subjects and express themselves with confidence. They learn a range of different instruments, styles of music, drama techniques and performance skills. Every child gets a chance to be in a public performance each year with the pre-prep nativity, and showcase and productions in prep. We have musical performances for Christmas, Harvest and other celebrations, and individual and group concerts for instrumentalists and singers. As well as this, drama is also incorporated into the pupils’ thematic work through forums such as class assemblies.
Additional clubs such as Prep School Choir and individual peripatetic music lessons allow children to follow their passions in our co-curricular offerings.
Senior Leadership Team
Led by Headmistress Rebecca Mitchell, Westonbirt Prep’s Senior Leadership Team provides strategic direction and ensures the school’s vision, values, and priorities are effectively implemented. The team includes senior leaders responsible for key areas such as teaching and learning, pastoral care, sport and learning support.
Working collaboratively, the Senior Leadership Team supports staff, monitors performance, and drives continuous improvement to create a safe, inclusive, and high-quality learning environment for all pupils at Westonbirt Prep.

pageCache.pageTitle: Westonbirt School scoops Co-Educational Independent School of the Year award and gains a five star review - Westonbirt School
pageCache.text:
Westonbirt School scoops Co-Educational Independent School of the Year award and gains a five star review
In September 2019 Westonbirt Senior School accepted its very first boys into Year 7, with boys also able to join Year 12 the year after. Four short – but intensely busy – years later, we are absolutely thrilled and very proud to announce that the School has won the Co-educational Independent School of the Year award, at the 2023 Independent Schools of the Year awards ceremony. More than 200 guests from 90 independent schools across the UK attended the event, which was run by Independent School Parent magazine and held at the Law Society in Chancery Lane, London on Tuesday October 10th.
The award recognises the huge journey that the School has undertaken in going co-ed, the vision and investment provided by Wishford Education and our backers to adapt and develop our School’s estate and facilities, the hard work and commitment from staff and the support from pupils and parents.
The major challenge over the last four years has been to manage the pace of change and growth effectively, despite the pandemic, and being situated in a Grade 1 listed building requiring adaptations to deliver education for boys. This year we have seen the fruits of that change and investment. including our new classrooms, a new astroturf, and Sports Hub. Across Years 7-11, boys now make up approximately 46% of our student numbers; we are truly a co-educational School, offering a fantastic experience and opportunities to both girls and boys.
We are very grateful to Independent School Parent for this allocade; we were up against some outstanding competition within this category, so it’s a great achievement to have won. Congratulations to all other finalists and winners, who all do such sterling work within the sector.
Westonbirt School was also named in the very first edition of the World’s Leading Boarding Schools 2023 Special Report by the US multinational business magazine Fortune, and Statista, a globally renowned market research firm.
This report is based on global surveys launched by Statista conducted with parents, alumni, boarding school advisors, heads of schools and heads of admissions and recognises the most highly recommended boarding schools around the world.
The leading boarding schools featured on this list have been assigned a five-star or four-star classification and Westonbirt received a five-star classification.

pageCache.pageTitle: Learning and Development - Specialist lessons & activities
pageCache.text:
Learning and Development
At Westonbirt Nursery, we offer a rich and diverse learning experience, including specialist-led activities, such as swimming. music, French, games and forest school to enrich our core curriculum and broaden children’s horizons.
In the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), play lies at the heart of our approach. We believe that through play, children develop essential life skills such as creativity, problem-solving, and social-emotional intelligence. Our experienced teachers carefully observe each child’s unique learning style and provide personalised support and challenging experiences to help them thrive.
Activities and Curriculum
At Westonbirt Nursery we follow the statutory guidance from the EYFS framework. This is supported by the non-statutory Development Matters. Nursery staff carefully observe each child, getting to know their interests, strengths and areas of development. Staff create a bespoke curriculum for each child, supporting them to develop across all seven areas of learning and development. Throughout their time at Nursery, children will be introduced to a range of festivals, events and new experiences.
In 2019, the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) rated Westonbirt as “excellent for academic achievement and pastoral care.” Inspectors noted that “in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), all children make very good progress in relation to their age and development. Pupils from the EYFS onwards have strong numeracy skills and enjoy their mathematics lessons.”
Nursery children play an active and valued role in many of the wider school events such as the swimming gala, sports day, the Harvest Festival and the Nativity play, exposing them to the enriching and rewarding experiences of Westonbirt from the start.
Specialist Teaching
Children in our Pre-School class, Peacocks, are offered numerous daily specialist lessons taught by specialist teachers from the Prep School. We are able to offer specialist teaching to nursery children in swimming, music, French, games and forest school. Attending these sessions is optional and is an additional cost. All children in our younger classes, Little Owls, Wrens and Robbins, participate in forest school.
Find out more and book a visit
Contact our Admissions Team to book a visit or taster session, or join us for our next Open Morning. This is an excellent opportunity to talk to the dedicated nursery staff about our ethos and educational provision and discuss how our flexible morning and afternoon sessions can best meet your needs. Find out more about joining our nursery via the link below.

pageCache.pageTitle: Outdoor Learning in Westonbirt School's vast grounds
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Learning
We are blessed with a vast amount of space and natural beauty at Westonbirt. As a school, we fully utilise our incredible surroundings to benefit children’s learning.
Whether it is dressing as ancient Greeks in the Italian Gardens, conducting science investigations in the meadow, cooking in the spinney during forest school, competing on the sports pitches or climbing and jumping in the play areas, outdoor activity plays a huge role in our school day.
An inspiring setting
We are very much an outdoor school and believe that the benefits of physical activity and fresh air are extremely important.
Our youngest children love learning in the Great Outdoors, and our pre-school classes in nursery and our pre-prep year groups all have a weekly lesson in our on-site Forest School.
For our older children, regular opportunities to extend their learning outdoors are given throughout the day and are included in our curriculum, extra-curricular clubs and activities and during recreation.
We encourage the children to learn, play and reflect in these inspiring spaces and to make the most of their learning and of their childhood.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep Sport in Prep School - Westonbirt School
pageCache.text:
Sport at Westonbirt Prep
Sport is a key part of our provision at Westonbirt Prep and plays vital role in every child’s journey at school.
As a school, we place emphasis on the holistic development of the player and sportsperson. This means that learning and refining the core skills required is vital and encouraged through the sessions but this sits alongside the values that sport brings such as: resilience; independence; teamwork; sportsmanship; courage and work ethic.
Children are encouraged to be competitive, determined and to give their all but at the same time to be evaluative of their performance, supportive of others, fair and most of all, to enjoy sport. Where children show a particular aptitude for sport, we will encourage and assist in their development and support them with their journey.
Sport Lessons
Every child at Westonbirt Prep from our pre-school class in Nursery to Year 6 will have a minimum of two sport lessons per week. Pre-school children take part in one 30-minute PE and one 30-minute Swimming lesson per week, while children in Reception to Year 6 take part in one PE, one Games and one Swimming lesson per week. Lessons for Reception to Year 6 last 55 minutes.
Children in Year 3 to Year 6 also take part in an additional Games fixtures afternoon every week, with teams competing in competitive matches and tournaments against other independent schools across the region. The growth of our competitive sport provision in recent years has allowed pupils opportunities to play in regional and national finals at professional sporting venues.
For Year 3 to Year 6 Games fixtures, rugby is the main sport of focus for boys in the Autumn Term, while girls play hockey. In the Spring Term, it is the boys’ turn to play hockey with the girls’ focus moving to netball. Cross-county is also an additional option for children in Year 3 and above in the first two terms. In the Summer Term, boys and girls all play mixed cricket and athletics. PE lessons for all year groups focus on wide range of sports, including football, badminton, gymnastics, lacrosse, tennis, cross-country and athletics.
Alongside this, children in Years 3 and above have access to additional tennis and golf lessons on site with specialist teachers, our invitation Swim Squad take part in weekly training sessions and regular galas, and the Westonbirt Equestrian Team compete in numerous events locally.
There is also the opportunity for children to take part in sports such as judo, fencing, archery and horse riding as part of our extensive after-school co-curricular options.
Swimming
Children from Nursery through to Year 6 are given the opportunity to swim every week right here at Westonbirt School. Every year group has at least one swim lesson a week all year round in our excellent indoor 25 metre pool. We focus on children initially learning water confidence and then develop pupils’ swimming across multiple strokes.
As children progress into Year 3 and above, there is an added competitive element where children are able to compete in galas. We have been very successfully in recent years, winning trophies on at a national level in the Olympic pool in London on multiple occasions.
Sporting Success
We have enjoyed growing sporting success in recent years, with impressive achievements at both national and regional level.
This success is led on the hockey pitch with our Under-11 Girls finishing as runners-up in the ISA National Hockey Finals in 2025, with the Under-11 Boys placing sixth. Both teams also finished runners-up at the Gloucestershire County Tournament to qualify for the South West Regional finals.
Also on the hockey pitch, our Under-9 Boys were crowned ISA South West Hockey champions in 2025, with the Under-9 Girls finishing as runners-up.
We have also had a strong number of pupils qualified for the ISA National Cross-Country, ISA National Athletics Finals and ISA National Swimming Finals over the past 12 months.
As part of the Wishford Group, we compete in numerous Wishford Competitions across the school year and are pleased to be the reigning champions in Athletics, Swimming and more.
Prep Sport Staff
Mr Tom Davies; Assistant Head – Sport and Co-Curricular
Westonbirt Prep’s sports department is led by Mr Tom Davies. Born into a sporting family, Mr Davies has been passionate about all sports from a young age. He represented his county in cricket and rugby at youth level; however, cricket was the sport he chose to specialise in, leading to six years in the Gloucestershire Cricket Academy and playing several County 2nd XI games, where he gained invaluable coaching and playing experience. Mr Davies joins Westonbirt from our sister school, Cricklade Manor Prep, where he served for 12 years, including the last 7 as Director of Sport. He has developed his coaching credentials and is an RFU Level 2 and ECB Level 2 coach.
Mrs Rachel Farmer; Head of Prep PE and Games
Mrs Farmer is the Head of Sport at Westonbirt Prep School and has been at Westonbirt for the last 6 years. Mrs Farmer graduated from the University of Birmingham with a degree in Sport, Physical Education and Coaching Sciences. She gained a Post Graduate Diploma in Secondary Education (QTS) specialising in Physical Education in 2011, before completing her Masters in Teaching Studies a few years later. She has always had a passion for sport; representing Somerset in cricket and taking on the role of Club Captain of the University of Birmingham Women’s Cricket Club. She plays regular competitive netball and was the Netball Coordinator for Team Bath.
Miss Adele Potts; Swim Lead for Nursery, Prep & Senior
Miss Potts was previously Acting Head of Swimming at Bishop’s Stortford College. Currently, Miss Potts is training in Stroud Masters and competing in triathlons; she swam in the 2-mile Swim Serpentine in September 2021. She has also a Senior Women’s record holder in 400 and 800m freestyle in the NW Open in Western Australia (2016). Swim England Coach member, Teaching Swimming and Water Safety and Teaching Towards Competitive Strokes accreditation (2018, AUSTSWIM, Australia) and UKCC Teaching Aquatics (2010).
Discover the full sport coaching team
Sports Facilities
Westonbirt boasts 210 acres of parkland grounds which provide the perfect platform for sporting excellence.
The school is home to its own Leisure Centre boasting an indoor 25m pool, sports hall and fitness suite. A nine-hole golf course is also located on site, while a full size floodlit Astro Turf pitch was recently opened and is used as a multi-purpose space by the sports department.
Tennis and netball courts are also available on site, while the extensive natural grounds provide the perfect location for rugby, lacrosse, football and cricket pitches.

pageCache.pageTitle: Westonbirt Sixth Form - preparing you for life beyond school
pageCache.text:
Academic Options
At Westonbirt Sixth Form, we believe these two years represent more than just a stepping stone to university, apprenticeships or careers – they are a time of real transformation. This is where young people grow into confident, independent thinkers ready to shape their futures and thrive beyond school. Our curriculum is both broad and ambitious, designed to inspire intellectual curiosity, creativity and resilience.
Subject Options
We offer a wide range of subjects and qualifications in Sixth Form, including A-Levels, BTECs, Leiths, the EPQ and more. Our broad and varied curriculum allows you to build a bespoke programme of study tailored to your interests and goals. Explore our full subject list below:
Subject Options
French
What are the aims of the course?
A Level French fosters articulate, culturally aware students who can communicate with confidence and insight. The course develops fluency in speaking and builds the ability to express ideas and opinions on current social and political issues. Students learn advanced vocabulary, grammatical accuracy, and the skills required to analyse spoken and written texts. Great emphasis is also given to debating ideas and to independent research, building transferable skills valued in higher education and international careers - ideal for ambitious, globally-minded students.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
To fully participate in the course we recommend students achieve a minimum Grade 6 in GCSE French.
Spanish
What are the aims of the course?
A Level Spanish offers students the chance to become confident and articulate speakers of one of the world’s most widely spoken languages. The course develops fluency, accuracy, and the ability to understand and discuss complex social, political, and cultural topics. By analysing original texts and expressing informed and nuanced opinions on topical issues, students grow in cultural awareness and analytical thinking. Research, debating, and extended writing are all key elements, laying the foundation for future academic study and global careers.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
We recommend a Grade 6 or above in GCSE Spanish to fully access the A Level course.
Religious Studies, Philosophy and Ethics
What are the aims of the course?
This thought-provoking course challenges students to explore life’s biggest questions: Does God exist? What is truth? How should we live? Students develop analytical and evaluative skills, confidence in debating complex ideas, and the ability to think independently and write persuasively. With passionate, expert teachers and excellent resources, students gain a deeper understanding of philosophy, ethics, and theology. Alongside deep subject knowledge, students also build valuable skills for university and beyond: critical thinking, essay writing, argument analysis, and independent learning – all in a supportive, inspiring environment.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
We recommend a Grade 6 or above in GCSE religious studies (or English if RS was not studied). However, more importantly, we are looking for students with curiosity, enthusiasm, and a genuine interest in big ideas and ethical challenges. Motivation and a willingness to think deeply are key.
Psychology
What are the aims of the course?
A Level psychology empowers students to explain behaviour through evidence, not opinion. Learn how memory works, why people conform, how the brain drives behaviour, and how mental health is understood and treated. Master research design, data analysis and evaluation, crafting clear, balanced arguments with strong written communication. The course builds ethical awareness, cultural sensitivity and scientific literacy so you can question claims, make informed decisions and apply psychological thinking to everyday life, further study and future careers.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
We recommend students achieve a Grade 6 in GCSE English language and mathematics; a Grade 5 in biology or combined science is also strongly recommended. A solid work ethic, regular reading and clear written expression are essential.
Physics
What are the aims of the course?
Building on (I)GCSE physics or GCSE combined science/IGCSE double award, A Level physics explores the nature, behaviour, and mathematics of the universe, from the subatomic to the cosmic, while studying the work of some of history’s greatest minds, including Einstein, Newton, Curie, and Bell. Students develop key skills in problem solving, reasoning, numeracy, ICT, and communication, while also examining the real-world applications and implications of physics. The subject complements many others, including mathematics, chemistry, biology, economics, technology/product design, computer science, and geography, and opens the door to a wide range of further study and career opportunities.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
Students will need to have achieved a Grade 6, or above, in (I)GCSE Physics, or GCSE combined science/IGCSE double award, as well as a Grade 6+ in (I)GCSE mathematics, in order to access the A Level physics course.
Music1
What are the aims of the course?
A Level music develops students’ skills and understanding in performing, composing, and appraising music, building upon their existing skills and introducing new techniques. The course encourages active engagement with music, developing confidence in performance and composition, and expands musical knowledge across a variety of styles and genres. Students will learn to analyse music from well-known composers, developing their analytical and appraising skills throughout the course.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
It is expected that students wishing to study A Level music have passed Grade 5 in at least one instrument or voice and have taken GCSE music.
Mathematics
What are the aims of the course?
The aim of A Level mathematics is to develop students’ understanding of mathematical concepts, methods, and techniques, while enhancing their problem-solving and analytical skills. It encourages logical reasoning, precision, and the ability to construct and communicate rigorous mathematical arguments. The course builds fluency in core topics such as algebra, calculus, and trigonometry, and applies mathematics to real-world contexts through statistics and mechanics. It prepares students for higher education, particularly in STEM fields, and supports a wide range of careers. Overall, it fosters confidence, curiosity, and appreciation for the role of mathematics in both academic and everyday life.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
To study A Level mathematics students need to achieve a minimum of a Grade 7 at GCSE.
Leiths School of Food and Wine
What are the aims of the course?
A bespoke Leith's cooking course, the curriculum and lessons are designed to build practical skills and confidence in planning, preparing and cooking a wide range of menus. Successful completion will enable students to join the Leiths list; an exclusive list of Leiths accepted and qualified individuals providing access to a variety of catering & hospitality jobs worldwide.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
There are no specific entry requirements although basic cookery skills are an advantage.
Latin
What are the aims of the course?
Studying Latin at A Level is a chance to understand the Roman language and literary culture in great depth, expanding upon learnings at GCSE. The course aims to develop translation skills and in particular literary analysis; examining authorial intent and rhetorical or poetic skill. There is even the chance to try Latin composition! Beyond Latin, students learn invaluable transferable skills such as extrapolating and conveying abstract material, attention to detail and critical thinking.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
You will need a Grade 7 or higher in GCSE Latin to study the subject at A Level.
History
What are the aims of the course?
The A Level history course aims to deepen understanding of key historical periods and develop critical analytical skills. Explore political, social, and economic developments across time in all three examined units. Students will learn how to evaluate sources for reliability, provenance, and context. The course also strengthens the ability to assess and construct historical interpretations using evidence and argument. The course will develop skills in critical thinking, independent research, extended writing, and forming substantiated judgments. These skills are essential for higher education and careers requiring analysis, communication, and decision-making; and encourages a thoughtful, questioning approach to the past and present.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
Students will need a Grade 6 at GCSE history (or English if they haven’t studied GCSE history) to study history at A Level.
Geography
What are the aims of the course?
Geography helps students understand how our world works, physically, socially, economically, and politically. The course explores key global issues such as climate change, urbanisation, resource use, and inequality, while also examining how these impact people and places at a local level. Students will consider processes and patterns over space and time, developing an understanding of how places change. Along the way, students build valuable skills in analysis, evaluation, decision-making, data interpretation, and extended writing, essential for university and beyond.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
Students must have a Grade 6 or above in GCSE geography. It is also advised to have at least a Grade 6 in both maths and English, as the course involves data interpretation, extended writing, and critical analysis.
Further Mathematics
What are the aims of the course?
Further A Level mathematics aims to deepen and broaden students’ mathematical knowledge beyond the standard A Level course. It covers advanced topics such as complex numbers, matrices, differential equations, and further calculus, encouraging the development of problem-solving, logical reasoning, and abstract thinking skills. The course promotes exploration of sophisticated mathematical ideas and techniques, helping students gain a stronger understanding of both theoretical and applied mathematics. It also fosters an appreciation for the elegance and power of mathematics, building confidence and independence in handling complex problems and real-world applications across various mathematical fields.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
To study A Level further mathematics students need to achieve a minimum of a Grade 8 at GCSE.
Agriculture
What are the aims of the course?
The agricultural sector is arguably the most important in the world; no farmers, no food, no future. Students who study this course will gain an insight into this global industry and will be equipped with skills that will set them above their peers. Students may indeed wish to go on to study an Agriculture BSc and other related degrees, but this course also complements the subjects of those who wish to study veterinary medicine, biosciences, business management and engineering degrees to name a few.
Entry Requirements
You will need a minimum Grade 4 in GCSE mathematics and English to undertake the course.
Extended Certificate in Sport
What are the aims of the course?
The BTEC Extended Certificate course is aimed at students who have a passion for sport and are looking to follow careers such as sports performance, physiotherapy, teaching, or coaching. It is a two-year course and is the equivalent to one A Level. For students who are considering a sports related degree, the BTEC Extended Certificate combines well with subjects such as biology and psychology.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
We recommend a Grade 6 or above in GCSE physical education (or biology/combined science if PE was not studied). A passion for learning about sport is important.
English Literature
What are the aims of the course?
English Literature A Level will transport students through the ages, and across the world, to hear voices that grapple with the very concept of what it means to be human in complex societies and at pivotal moments in time. This course will develop analytical, critical and literacy skills that are highly flexible and transferrable. Students are encouraged to develop a personal relationship with texts and form their own critical opinions. Fundamentally, English Literature allows students to challenge conceptions about society and humanity and it enables them to explore the fascinating relationship between art, in the wider sense, and reality itself.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
To fully participate in the course a Grade 6 GCSE English Literature and a Grade 5 in English Language is recommended.
Economics
What are the aims of the course?
A Level economics aims to equip young people with the ability to think critically, analyse complex information, and make well-reasoned decisions. The course encourages logical thinking, effective communication, and the interpretation of data to build and evaluate arguments. Students develop problem-solving skills, an awareness of different perspectives, and the confidence to engage with real-world issues. These transferable skills prepare them for further study, active citizenship, and a wide range of future careers.
Are there any specific entry requirements?
We recommend a Grade 5 or above in both Maths and English.
Drama & Theatre
What are the aims of the course?
A Level drama and theatre invites students to immerse themselves in play texts while developing practical skills as an actor, designer, or director. A commitment to live theatre is at the heart of the course, enriching studies and sparking what may become a lifelong passion for theatre-going. Blending creative practice with theoretical exploration, this challenging yet deeply rewarding subject offers an unfo

Admissions at Westonbirt
Whether you’re exploring options for Nursery and Prep, looking at our dynamic Senior School, or just beginning your search, our experienced Admissions Team will support you every step of the way. From your first enquiry to your child’s first day, you’ll have a dedicated guide who knows that every child deserves to be known, encouraged and inspired to thrive.
Express your interest
Book a Personal Tour
Nothing compares to experiencing Westonbirt school life first hand and we’d love to welcome you for a visit. You’ll have the chance to explore our beautiful house and grounds, see our facilities in action, and meet with either our Prep or Senior Head to discuss what matters most to your family. It’s your opportunity to ask questions, get a real feel for our community, and discover how we can support your child’s journey.
Book a personal tour
Open Events
You can experience Westonbirt at one of our dedicated Open Events, where you’ll see our school community in action. Whether it’s an Open Morning, Open Door day, Teddy Bears’ Picnic, or boarding taster event, each offers a unique insight into life and learning here. You’ll meet our staff and pupils, observe lessons first hand, and discover what makes our school special.
Find out more about upcoming events here:
The Admissions Process
We’re here to make the admissions process as straightforward as possible, and our friendly Admissions Team is always on hand to help. The journey looks slightly different depending on whether your child is joining our Nursery, Prep School or Senior School. Use the links below to see what to expect at each stage.
Nursery Joining Information
Prep Admissions Process
Senior & Sixth Form Admissions Process
International Admissions Process
International Programme
Westonbirt has been welcoming students from across the world for over 100 years. Ours is a vibrant, international community where overseas students experience the very best of British education: high-quality academic learning, beautiful boarding facilities, and a stunning setting in 210 acres of Cotswold parklands.
HM Armed Forces
Westonbirt welcomes applications from HM Armed Forces personnel and the school community has included many forces families over the years.
Day Pupils of serving members of HM Forces are eligible for a reduction in fees of up to 10%, subject to parents’ circumstances. Full Boarding students of serving members of HM Forces at Westonbirt pay 10% of the full fees so long as they are in receipt of the Continuity of Education Allowance (CEA).
Please do not hesitate to contact our admissions team to further discuss opportunities for HM Armed Forces personnel.

Welcome to Westonbirt Nursery
Through free play, formal learning and great outdoor experiences, Westonbirt Nursery encourages creativity, curiosity, confidence and fun – as well as a lifelong love for learning and exploring. Our core programme is supplemented by a range of exciting and dynamic extra-curricular activities that are led by specialist teachers including music, French, games, swimming and forest school.
Meet The Head
Westonbirt Nursery welcomes children from 2 years through to pre-school. The Nursery is a vibrant and positive setting where the happiness of the children is our priority. The location allows for extensive use of our wonderful outdoor space and exploring nature and the wider world is a large part of the Westonbirt experience.
Children learn primarily through play and follow the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum; they begin to build their understanding of numbers, sounds and language with daily sessions that build through their time with us from 2 years old to the preparation for transition to school phase. This phase focuses on giving the children an opportunity to develop independence and confidence, as well as key skills such as writing, holding cutlery, getting themselves changed and following routines and expectations.
The school aims of Curiosity, Creativity and Courage are prevalent in all that happens in Nursery and this stands children in good stead to move on in their educational journey.
Contact our admissions team to book a taster session or join us for our next Open Day. This is an excellent opportunity to talk to the dedicated nursery staff about our ethos and educational provision and discuss how our flexible morning and afternoon sessions can best meet your needs:
Q & A
How old must my child be to attend Westonbirt Nursery?
Westonbirt Nursery is open to children aged 2-4 years old.
Is parking available at Westonbirt Nursery?
Westonbirt School's main car park is located next to Westonbirt Nursery. Dedicated drop-off bays for Westonbirt Prep and Westonbirt Nursery are also available for use in the morning and afternoon, located directly outside the nursery.
Does Westonbirt Nursery accept Government funding?
Westonbirt Nursery accept up to 15 hours’ free childcare entitlement per week for up to 38 weeks of the year. For those registered for term-time only, we offer 15 hours per week for the total weeks attended. Those registered for a year-round place will receive their free hours pro-rated over the three funding periods (1st Sept – 31st Dec; 1st Jan – 31st Mar; 1st Apr – 31st Aug). We also accept childcare vouchers to pay for nursery care.
What time does Westonbirt Nursery open and close?
Westonbirt Nursery is open from 8am-6pm, Monday to Friday.
Is Westonbirt Nursery open all year round?
Westonbirt Nursery year runs from September to August. We accept pupils for either school term time only or for the whole year. Term time only pupils may book additional ad-hoc nursery sessions during the school holidays, subject to places being available.
What is the minimum number of sessions I can book at Westonbirt Nursery?
We require a minimum attendance of 2 full days per week to join the nursery.
Is food included in Westonbirt Nursery fees?
Westonbirt Nursery fees include all food and consumables required to support our provision. We also offer a wide range of activities during the nursery week; these are all included in the session rates where these are paid. If using free childcare entitlement, you will be asked to pay towards the cost of food and consumables, and for some activities where funding does not meet the cost. Please view our full Nursery Fees Information here.
How do I visit Westonbirt Nursery?
Contact our Admissions Team via nurseryadmissions@westonbirtschool.uk or 01666 881400 to book a individual visit to Westonbirt Nursery. You can also register to attend our Prep School and Nursery Open Mornings, which take place in the autumn and spring.
